item.title: WinUI 3 developer-community digest — October 6, 2026
item.description: WinUI 3 developer-community digest — October 6, 2026 Primary window: October 5, 8:30 a.m. → October 6, 8:30 a.m. PDT. Seven-day catch-up: September 29 → October 6; initial complete-coverage baseline remains open. Archive: Today’s takeaways TransformToVisual retention now has a second developer’s reproduction across SDK 2.4.0 and 2.5.1; earlier default-heap-only measurements missed most of the growth. The recent MSIX build-tools error is explained as Visual Studio retaining an old task DLL after upgrading packages. Restarting VS is suggested; cache cleanup is the reporter-tested workaround. A long-standing x:Bind null-argument bug is fixed in merged source. No released package containing that compiler change was verified. Community experience MSIX build failure gains an explanation—and a lighter workaround to try. WindowsAppSDK issue, opened October 4; new reply October 5, 11:57 a.m. PDT.

item.description: WinUI 3 developer digest — October 3, 2026 Archive: Revised October 3, 13:58 PDT; collection cutoff 13:57:00 PDT. Latest-day focus: Oct 2, 13:57:00 → Oct 3, 13:57:00 PDT. Seven-day catch-up: Sept 26–Oct 3, continuing partial initial coverage. Useful verified stories from this morning are retained, with earlier-window activity labeled separately. A shipping community control fills another gap: RibbonSpace now supports plain WinUI 3, with concrete porting lessons. Search works, source access still doesn't: DuckDuckGo surfaced human Stack Overflow Q&A, but blocked originals and unverified dates prevent treating snippets as new fixes. item.title: WinUI 3 developer-community digest — October 2, 2026
item.description: WinUI 3 developer-community digest — October 2, 2026 Coverage: October 1, 08:30 → October 2, 08:30 PDT. Seven-day catch-up searches; previously reported stories excluded. Overall coverage is partial. Takeaways Packaging gets tangible fixes: a published MSIX BuildTools update addresses resource/publish failures—not merely a promised source change. Practical gotchas: scope WindowsAppSDKSelfContained to the executable, and don’t equate successful notification calls with visible toasts. Input performance: fresh ColorPicker reports implicate high mouse polling rates; users provide a mitigation and debugging evidence, not a confirmed framework fix. Community experience SimpleFiles: a student ships a native file manager. Reddit r/SideProject, October 1.
